clue.text: Not coy, working for magnate

indicators.note: letters that are working are set in motion and moved about, so the preceding words get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone shy decides to stop being bashful and go to work for a business tycoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A tycoon is a wealthy, powerful businessman, which is exactly what a magnate is: a straight synonym.

clue.text: Facetious language followed by creep with cry of mock horror

parts.note: a tongue is a language
to inch is to creep slowly forward
eek is a comic squeal of fright

explanation.surface: Joking talk that is followed by a sneaky person shrieking in pretend alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creep' reads as a noun for an unpleasant person but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue-in-cheek describes something said ironically and not seriously, which is what facetious means.

clue.text: Controlled a nervous movement up in fortress

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: led means directed or controlled
taken as written
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A twitchy soldier is kept in check inside a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortified stronghold, typically guarding a city, so it is a synonym for fortress.

clue.text: Willows and wild roses covering island

indicators.note: covering something means wrapping around it, so one element goes inside
wild letters are out of control and scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Willow trees and wild roses growing over an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiers are a kind of willow whose flexible shoots are used in basket-making, so they are examples.

clue.text: Man in supreme command

indicators.note: one word sitting in another means it goes inside it

parts.note: the best is the supreme one
a man is referred to as he

explanation.surface: Reads like a description of a man holding the highest rank of authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supreme command' looks like one phrase but splits: supreme is wordplay, command alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is an order or instruction, as in 'at the king's behest', so it is a noun synonym for command.

clue.text: Wash tub's last two articles

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter
a and the are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: Instructions for washing a tub, or a list of its contents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tub's last two' tempts you to take two letters; 'two' belongs with articles.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to wash oneself or something by immersing it in water, so it is a verb synonym.

clue.text: Corruption of demon has to be substantial

indicators.note: corrupted letters are spoiled and twisted out of their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A devil's corrupting influence must be considerable.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome can mean large or generous, as in a handsome profit, which is a sense of substantial.

clue.text: Learner in boat endlessly going over tips from unconventional expert

indicators.note: the learner is in the boat, so one goes inside the other
endlessly means without its end, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: a skiff is a small rowing boat
L for learner, as on L-plates

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its two ends

parts.note: the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A novice in a small boat capsizes, guided by an unusual expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expert' seems to belong with 'unconventional', but only that word's tips are used; expert alone is the definition. In a down clue, 'going over' means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilful is an adjective for someone with great ability, and expert used adjectivally means the same.

clue.text: Bird in display filled with passion

indicators.note: something filled with another has it placed inside

parts.note: to wear something is to display it, as in wearing a smile
heat is intensity of feeling, as in the heat of the moment

explanation.surface: A bird performing a courtship display full of ardour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Display' looks like a noun for a bird's courtship show, but it is the verb, as in wearing a smile.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheatear is a small migratory songbird with a white rump, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Despite reputation, getting behind idiot in drama

indicators.note: the first element comes behind the second, so it is placed after it
the idiot is placed in the drama, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese drama
a twit is a fool
one's standing is one's reputation

explanation.surface: Someone's good name survives even though an idiot features in the play.
explanation.walkthrough: Noh is a stylised form of classical Japanese theatre, a crossword favourite for drama.
explanation.definitionFit: Notwithstanding is a formal preposition meaning in spite of, so it swaps directly for despite.

clue.text: Feminist from different era emerging with hesitation

indicators.note: a different version of the letters is a rearranged one

parts.note: taken as written
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A campaigner for women's rights appears from another time, rather tentatively.
explanation.definitionFit: Germaine Greer is the Australian author of The Female Eunuch and a leading figure of second-wave feminism.

clue.text: Less than appropriate promise

parts.note: under means less than, as in under ten
to appropriate something is to take it

explanation.surface: Suggests a pledge that falls short of what would be fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective describing the promise, but it is the verb meaning seize.
explanation.definitionFit: To undertake to do something is to pledge or commit oneself to it, a verb sense matching promise.

clue.text: Arbiter, since retiring, in less danger

indicators.note: retiring means going back or withdrawing, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a referee, or ref, arbitrates a game
as can mean since, as in 'as it was late'

explanation.surface: A referee who has stepped down from officiating is now less at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: Safer is the comparative of safe, meaning more secure or less exposed to harm, which matches the phrase.

clue.text: Find clue with odd parts missing? That's useless

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even-positioned ones

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A solver complains that a clue with strange bits left out is pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can describe something futile or without purpose, as in idle threats, so it means useless.

clue.text: Pal became excited about hot dessert

indicators.note: about means around, so the other letters surround one element
excited letters are stirred up and moved out of order

parts.note: taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A friend gets worked up over a warm pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Peach Melba is a classic dessert of peaches, vanilla ice cream and raspberry sauce, so it is an example.

clue.text: Examinations inhibit us, keeping quiet

parts.note: to check is to restrain

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it within, so it goes inside

parts.note: taken as written
p is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Medical tests make people nervous, so they keep their voices down.
explanation.definitionFit: Check-ups are routine examinations, especially medical or dental ones, so the plural nouns match.

clue.text: Wise to restrict pressure before bad overflow

indicators.note: restricting something holds it in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: a sage is a wise person, and sage also means wise

indicators.note: before puts one element ahead of the next in the order read

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: Sensible advice to limit pressure before something nasty bursts out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wise' is an adjective but stands for a word that is both adjective and noun for a wise person.
explanation.definitionFit: Spillage is liquid that has spilled over its container, which is a kind of overflow.

clue.text: Songwriter taking firm line with journalist, right away

indicators.note: sending something away takes it out of the word

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company
L is a standard abbreviation for line
a reporter is a journalist
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A composer is stern with a reporter and then marches off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' reads as immediately, but it means the letter for right is sent away from the journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole Porter was an American composer of standards like Night and Day, so he is an example of a songwriter.

clue.text: Characters in correspondence

definitions.meaning: first meaning: symbols of the alphabet
second meaning: written messages sent by post

explanation.surface: People who appear in an exchange of written messages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' suggests people in a story, but here it means alphabet symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the symbols of an alphabet and the written messages people send through the post.

clue.text: Stagger, being wounded — not good

indicators.note: not means without, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: stung means hurt or wounded
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone reels about after being injured, and it is not looking good.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to astonish or shock them, the same verb sense as stun.

clue.text: Test involving iodine, very little

indicators.note: involving means including, so other letters are taken inside

parts.note: a trial is a test
I is the chemical symbol for iodine
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A chemistry experiment that uses only a tiny amount of iodine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very little' reads as one phrase; very is V in the wordplay and little alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial means of small importance or amount, so it fits little in the sense of slight or minor.

clue.text: Sombre doctor stood up

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
rose is the past tense of rise, to get to one's feet

explanation.surface: A gloomy physician got to their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' tempts you to read letters backwards, but 'stood up' is simply the past tense of rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means gloomy and sullen in mood, which is a direct synonym for sombre.

clue.text: Praise former partner with revolutionary group

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: Someone compliments an old flame who has joined a band of radicals.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly and enthusiastically, so it is a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Some junk now in garage in the dark

indicators.note: some of the following words means only part of their letters are used

parts.note: the letters run across these four words

explanation.surface: Pictures junk sitting in a garage with no light on.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the dark is an idiom for being unaware or uninformed, so it means unknowing.

clue.text: Engineer about to reveal submarine

indicators.note: to engineer something is to construct or contrive it, so the letters get rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A naval engineer is on the point of unveiling a new sub.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-boat is a German military submarine from the world wars, so it is a specific example.

clue.text: Avoid attracting attention of warlike people running riot

indicators.note: a crowd running riot scatters in disorder, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to stay unnoticed when aggressive folk are on the rampage.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a low profile is an idiom for staying out of sight and avoiding notice.

clue.text: Head for alpine trail to make this?

definitions.text: Head for alpine trail to make this?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter
a scent is a trail followed by hounds

explanation.surface: A hiker sets off on a mountain path to climb.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: heading for an alpine path, you make a climb.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a climb upward, the thing you make when you take a mountain trail in the Alps.

clue.text: Recall varied stock of wine

indicators.note: varied means changed, so the letters take a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Remembering a diverse collection of wines.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar can mean the collection of wines someone keeps, not just the underground room storing them.
